close_reason: Public-API change: ClientError::InvalidArgument from free-form String to structured data. Variant shape change requires major version. Coordinate with bd:JMAP-6lsm.21 (same shape concern in base-client errors) — both deferred to 0.2.0.
description:
Every guard returns:
```
return Err(jmap_base_client::ClientError::InvalidArgument(
    "calendar_get: ids element may not be empty".into(),
));
```

The `InvalidArgument(String)` variant of ClientError (defined in LOCKED jmap-base-client/src/error.rs) wraps a free-form description. Callers cannot:
- Distinguish 'empty id' from 'bad UTF-8 in token' from 'colon in BasicAuth username'
- Programmatically test which argument was bad
- Do anything other than match the variant and log/show the string

This is a downstream library limitation (jmap-base-client is locked). Inside calendars-client we can mitigate by being consistent about error message format — every guard already prefixes with `<method>: <field> <constraint>`. Good. But callers who want to handle 'invalid because of empty id list' specifically cannot.

Not actionable as a calendars-client fix without changing locked base-client. Flag for the eventual base-client review/unlock cycle: split InvalidArgument into a structured variant with field name + reason.
title: ClientError::InvalidArgument carries free-form String, not structured error data
